text:
Sara: Quick sync — thinking through a simplified "stable headroom" approach for Dedicated GPU pools. Wanted to float the idea before I write an RFC.
Mike: Love it, give us the 1-liner.
Sara: Keep a small, predictable reserved headroom per pool that decays slowly; allow an ephemeral burst lane backed by a debt/credit ledger. Admission checks consult headroom first, then burst if budget permits.
Tony: So headroom = allocation we never touch unless forced? How do we pick size?
Sara: Headroom targets are SLO-driven: e.g., 99th latency SLA aims -> headroom = function(p95 warmup cost, inflight variance). Start with % of pool GPUs for conservative rollout.
Jia: We should avoid hard pins. Suggest a smoothing window: headroom decays on inactivity over N minutes and replenishes over M minutes. That avoids sharp capacity swings.
Mike: What about fairness across tenants when burst consumes headroom? We need a preemption contract.
Tony: Preemption + graceful drain. If tenant A is on ephemeral burst and someone uses reserved, A gets 10s warning then moved to lower QOS lane or paused.
Alexa: Ops question — how do we surface this in Console? Need metrics: headroom_used, burst_balance_by_tenant, preemptions, admission_latency.
Sara: Agreed. Also telemetry hooks for adaptive controller: time-series of admission decisions, queue length, queue age, and token cost per request.
Mike: Can we show a minimal admission pseudo-proto?
Sara: Sure:
```
admit(request) -> {
  if pool.free_capacity >= request.size: grant
  else if pool.headroom.available >= request.size: consume_headroom_and_grant
  else if tenant.burst_balance >= cost_estimate: debit_burst_and_grant_with_burst_flag
  else: deny_or_enqueue
}
```
Tony: Where does the operator live? autoscaler vs pool-operator? We should keep admission local to pool-operator and let autoscaler adjust headroom params async.
Jia: That separation sounds good: pool-operator handles immediate admits/preempts; autoscaler writes desired headroom via CRD and relies on measurement loop.
Mike: Rollout plan? Feature flag + canary pools then global. We need safe defaults to avoid mass headroom drain.
Sara: Plan: 1) implement admission + metrics behind ff; 2) enable on 2 non-prod pools for 48h traffic replay; 3) canary on a small prod pool for 24h; 4) global with slow ramp.
Alexa: Add an alert: sustained preemptions > X per minute triggers rollback. Also billing hooks — burst debt should be visible on tenant billing page.
Tony: Edge case — prolonged high load exhausting headroom repeatedly. Autoscaler should attempt reactive scale, but budget floor prevents oscillations. Add cooldown and backoff.
Jia: Also add a probe/measurement job: small synthetic requests to estimate warmup penalty per model/slot so headroom sizing improves over time.
Mike: Nice. Any concerns about telemetry volume? We're adding a lot.
Sara: Keep high-cardinality metrics as sampled logs; aggregate counters for dashboards.
Alexa: I'll sketch dashboard tiles: headroom % used, burst debt, avg admit latency, preemptions.
scale-bot: [autoscaler-sim] ran 1k sims with current policy; median tail-latency improved 12%, but tail variance increased for 3 small tenants — recommend conservative initial headroom.
Sara: Thanks @scale-bot. Action items: Sara write RFC with above, Jia to draft probe job, Alexa dashboard mocks, Mike/Tony to scope operator separation and CRD fields. I'll open the RFC today. :+1:
Mike: Thanks — ping when RFC is up, happy to review.
Tony: I'll sketch the preemption state machine.
Jia: Will prototype probe runner this week.
Alexa: Will add dashboard PR once metrics names are finalized.
Sara: Cool. Closing this thread once RFC link posted.
